source_manifest: hand-written app-manifest.json in the § 3.3 shape (the instance's own site; Lane C runs in parallel)

jobs.statement: When I hear about HeyHi, I want to read its writing, so I can judge the thinking.
When I land on the site, I want to see what HeyHi is, so I can decide if it is for me.
When something resonates, I want to follow new writing, so I do not have to check back.
When I want to see the work rather than read about it, I want to explore the interactive lab.

flows.name: Read then follow
flows.trigger: the subscribe link in home's Contact section (leads to the external Substack)

encoded_decisions.decision: An entry is publicly visible only when its published flag is exactly true; file existence never equals visibility.
The publication gate is strict: any value other than the literal true (including the string 'True') keeps the entry hidden.
The site takes no lead capture: a direct email and a subscribe link, no form. It is a place to read, not a funnel.
A published slug is stable; changing it requires a 301 redirect in vercel.json.
The frontmatter parser avoids eval and new Function so the production bundle is CSP-safe.

vocabulary.meaning: The site's writing index and its entries.
The interactive experiments surface, distinct from the Log.
A Log post, typed essay or observation.
An internal T1 to T5 tag carried on an entry.
A named resource surface on the site.

constraints.constraint: Any surface that lists or renders an entry must obey the published === true visibility gate.
A new feature must not add a lead-capture form to the site; the no-funnel posture is deliberate.
A feature that changes a published slug must ship a 301 redirect in vercel.json.
No feature may introduce eval or new Function into the production bundle.
